clue.text: A bit of chicken for currying

definitions.meaning: the fleshy red crest on a fowl's head
currying a horse means grooming it with a brush or ...

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a piece of chicken to put in a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel's red crest is its comb; to curry a horse is to groom it, which is combing its coat.

clue.text: He's prepared to dispatch modern furniture

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era of dates
a dresser is a kitchen cupboard with shelves

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to send off some contemporary furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes the destination on a letter or parcel readies it for posting.

clue.text: Meadow Way would appear the shortest

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
St, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A remark that Meadow Way is the briefest road around.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallest in amount or length; the least distance is the shortest one.

clue.text: A quarter of the quiz will be most undemanding

parts.note: S, south, is one quarter of the compass
taken as written
a test is a quiz

explanation.surface: One section of the quiz will turn out to be the easiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft can mean easy or undemanding, as in a soft option.

clue.text: Boss getting on with the episcopate

parts.note: over and on both mean above, upon
a see is a bishop's office or diocese

explanation.surface: A church manager getting along well with the bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: To boss is to supervise or manage, a verb sense.

clue.text: Spruce can be cut back

explanation.surface: Advice that a fir tree may be pruned.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce as an adjective means neat and tidy; to cut back hair or a hedge is to clip it.

clue.text: A revolting fellow put to flight

definitions.meaning: a man who rises in revolt
the vertical part of a step, set into a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A rebel chased away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel rises against authority; the upright board of each step on a staircase is built into a flight of stairs.

clue.text: The cars men use in town

indicators.note: put to use, these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The vehicles that men drive around a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' signals the anagram of THE CARS MEN; 'in' is a link. MANCHESTER is a large city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in north-west England, loosely a big urban place.

clue.text: Egghead people ring when making changes

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word egg
men are people
ding is the sound of a bell ringing

explanation.surface: An intellectual's people phone when they alter things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Emending is correcting or revising a text.

clue.text: Agencies aimed to effect reform

indicators.note: the letters of the word aimed are reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Organisations intending to bring about change.
explanation.definitionFit: Press, television and radio are channels of mass communication, the means through which things are done.

clue.text: Prodigal son holds mum he's pledged to help

indicators.note: the pair of words prodigal and son wrap around the word for mother

parts.note: free with money, lavish
taken as written
ma is mother

explanation.surface: The prodigal son keeps quiet about promising to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' reads as keeping quiet, but here it is the word for mother; 'holds' puts it inside the prodigal son.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Masonic fraternity takes an oath to aid fellow members.

clue.text: Get together with the head, all being comme il faut

parts.note: to meet is to get together
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Meeting the headteacher with everything proper and correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old word for fitting or proper, so this is propriety, the quality of being correct.

clue.text: The prime minister no longer takes the point

explanation.surface: A former premier making a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was British prime minister from 1770 to 1782, during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North led the British government in the 1770s; one of the four cardinal compass points is at the top.

clue.text: A supporter catching favoured train

indicators.note: the word for supporter catches, or holds, the word for favoured

parts.note: a disciple is a follower or supporter
in means in favour, popular

explanation.surface: A fan grabbing a train he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the railway; it is the verb, to drill or school.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to drill or school them, which is to instil order.

clue.text: Certain sightless people have acute perception

indicators.note: the run of words certain sightless has the letters within it

explanation.surface: Some blind people have keen intuition.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across certaIN SIGHTless.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep understanding or discernment, a sharp grasp of the truth.

clue.text: Sort of rare gems obtainable in Cumbria

indicators.note: the letters of rare gems are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of precious stone found in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASMERE is a lake and village in Cumbria, in England's Lake District, home of Wordsworth.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lake District village and lake in north-west England.

clue.text: Tired, so maybe reading the newspaper leaders

indicators.note: suggests the letters of tired so could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Weary, so perhaps reading the paper's opinion columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' tempts toward editorials; it means the people in charge of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who run a paper and decide its content are its chiefs.

clue.text: William's backers bringing order into augury

indicators.note: the word for order is brought into the word for augury

parts.note: an omen is a sign of the future
a range is a row or ordered series

explanation.surface: King William's supporters bringing discipline to fortune-telling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order, a Protestant society in Northern Ireland, honours William III, William of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a Protestant society named after William of Orange, who backed his cause.

clue.text: Showing concern about horse butchery

indicators.note: the word for concern goes around the word for horse

parts.note: care is concern
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Being worried about the slaughter of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale slaughter, a massacre.

clue.text: The all-round squeeze

parts.note: a squeeze that goes all the way round someone, arms encircling them

explanation.definitionFit: A hug wraps the arms right round another person.

clue.text: One doesn't feel obliged to find where the fire is

definitions.meaning: inside the iron basket of a fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone ungrateful looking for the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person feels no obligation; split, the letters say located inside the hearth's iron basket.

clue.text: Writes-not all find it especially difficult

indicators.note: only part of the words find it especially is used

explanation.surface: A complaint that some people struggle to write.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fIND IT ESpecially; 'difficult' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To indite is an old word for composing or putting into words.

clue.text: Formal accommodation for a Trojan ruler

indicators.note: the word for formal accommodates, or holds, the letter a

parts.note: prim is stiff and formal

explanation.surface: Proper lodgings for a king of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Priam was king of Troy during the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Troy in Greek legend, father of Hector and Paris.

clue.text: The rogue heading the Spanish force

indicators.note: the rogue comes at the head, in front of the other piece

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: The villain leading the Spanish army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' looks like a military unit but is the verb, to drive or compel.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or compel someone to act.

clue.text: Teasing can get offensive in time

parts.note: bad can mean nasty or offensive
taken as written
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Mocking can become hurtful over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful banter, witty joking talk.

clue.text: Dark and dreadful thing

indicators.note: a dreadful state suggests the letters of thing are mangled

explanation.surface: A gloomy and frightful creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark as a noun means nightfall, the hours without daylight.

clue.text: Note for example ascending falcon

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: say means for example

explanation.surface: A remark about a bird of prey rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hawk taken from the nest for training in falconry.

clue.text: Mean with a conservationist body —— so critical

parts.note: import is meaning, significance, as a verb to mean
taken as written
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Unkind behaviour by an environmental group, which matters greatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Crucial or vital, of great consequence.

clue.text: In high spirits about midsummer game

indicators.note: the word for high spirits goes around the middle letters

parts.note: gay in its old sense of merry
the middle of the word summer is MM

explanation.surface: Cheerful about a summer festival game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a sport but means lame, as a game leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A game leg is lame or injured, the same as a gammy one.

clue.text: A woman from the Orient, wholly retiring

parts.note: E is east, the Orient

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: all means wholly

explanation.surface: A shy lady from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in Ella Fitzgerald.

clue.text: Information kiosks

parts.note: booths where papers bringing the latest reports are sold

explanation.definitionFit: Stalls selling papers and magazines on the street.
